A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RPM framework. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: V4 reports original benchmark experiments, ablations, human evaluations, retrieval analyses, and cross-model experiments in Section 4 and Appendix E.

after.justification: V5 retains those original results and adds structured reasoning comparisons, a verbosity analysis, and a human hallucination audit in Appendices E.6–E.8.

M1.justification: Feature extraction, factor construction, reasoning-memory construction, and feature-based retrieval remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 adds the factor set Cu to target-query feature extraction, matching the factor-aware procedure already described in v4 Section 3.4; this corrects documentation rather than establishing a new procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same movie-tagging, product-rating, scholarly-title-generation, and country-level opinion-prediction tasks using LaMP-2, LaMP-3, LaMP-5, and GOQA. The new analyses examine outputs within this retained coverage.

E2.justification: V5 Appendix E.6 and Table 11 add Structured Preference Induction and ToT-style prompting across the four retained benchmarks. This is a bounded extension of the comparator set; existing comparisons, including HYDRA + CoT, remain.

E3.justification: Core benchmark splits, metrics, backbones, and retrieval settings remain unchanged. V5 adds protocols for longest-explanation preference analysis and a two-annotator audit of 200 reasoning paths, nominally 50 per dataset. Appendix D.4 also expands the stated faithfulness criterion to include final-answer consistency, without establishing that the original evaluation was rerun.

E4.justification: Appendices E.7–E.8 add two distinct investigations absent from v4: whether verbosity biases human reasoning preferences and whether reasoning paths mention features or factors absent from their input context. These substantially extend scrutiny of reasoning reliability beyond the retained preference, component-validity, ablation, and transfer analyses.

E5.justification: V5 adds Cohen’s h for the verbosity analysis, explanation-length standard deviations in Table 12, and inter-annotator agreement in Table 13. Table 5 already reports standard deviations over three runs in v4 and remains unchanged; no increase in repeated runs is established.

E6.justification: Existing numerical tables and figure results are retained. New supplementary results include GOQA scores of 0.777 for Structured Preference Induction and 0.806 for ToT-style prompting in Table 11, explanation-length statistics in Table 12, and reported overall hallucination rates of 3.5% and 4.75% in Table 13.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations for factor statistics and retrieval remain unchanged, with no new theoretical results or proofs. Table 4 corrects coverage’s description from a fraction to a count, matching the counting definition already present in v4 Equation 2.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction refine RPM’s novelty around automatic discovery of user-specific reasoning structures and explicitly distinguish it from generic CoT/ToT strategies. The contribution list also highlights cross-model transferability. The central personalization, performance, and interpretability claims and the conclusion remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix F adds specific limitations concerning unrelated target domains and fixed factor sets lacking reconstruction triggers. V5 also adds interpretations that transfer overrides model self-bias, verbosity does not explain human preferences, and structured grounding reduces hallucinations; these extend the earlier interpretations.

D1.justification: V5 supplies a concrete public-code repository link in the abstract, whereas v4 only refers generally to provided code. It also makes factor conditioning explicit in Algorithm 1 and clarifies preprocessing-cost coverage. Existing hardware, model-version, clustering-parameter, and prompt disclosures remain.

R1.justification: V5 adds Cheng et al. (2023), Zhang and Chen (2020), and Zhang et al. (2014) to motivate factor statistics, plus Yao et al. (2023) for ToT-style reasoning. It sharpens positioning against generic structured reasoning while retaining the existing related-work organization.

P1.justification: V5 makes localized language and explanatory revisions, converts the contribution paragraph into bullets, and adds ethics, reproducibility, acknowledgments, and LLM-usage sections. The main narrative remains intact; the prompt and case-study appendices move from G/H to H/I.

P2.justification: V5 adds three supplementary tables, numbered 11–13, and renumbers subsequent prompt and case-study tables. Existing figures retain their content, while tables and figures shift with text reflow. The conference header replaces the preprint header.

improvement.justification: V5 adds useful comparison coverage, code-access information, and concrete limitations. However, its new verbosity analysis claims 200 LaMP-5 examples despite Appendix D.4 specifying 50, and Table 13 reports a 9% hallucination rate despite specifying 50 binary judgments per dataset. These unresolved inconsistencies weaken the principal new empirical evidence, leaving the net effect on overall paper quality uncertain.
